title: Buying on offer without filling the back room
target: How to use the wholesale offers and the discounts in Supermarket Simulator deliberately: what an offer actually is, where it is announced, how it differs from a discount, and when buying in bulk is worth the space it takes.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shop with stock space to spare
A rough idea of what sells

steps.do: Look at the offer before you place the order rather than after it arrives, because wholesale runs through a manager and settings of its own.
steps.because: wholesale offers run through a manager and settings of their own (WholeSaleManager, WholeSaleSettingsSO)

steps.do: Check that wholesale is turned on at all before you wait for an offer.
steps.because: the system keeps a switch for wholesale and for wholesale orders (isWholeSale, enableWholesaleOrders)

steps.do: Read the kind of offer as well as the price, because an offer carries a kind and may be a buying offer rather than a selling one.
steps.because: offers carry a kind and can be buying offers (OfferType, isBuyOffer)

steps.do: Watch the clock: an offer has a time limit of its own rather than lasting until you take it.
Accept deliberately, because accepting is a step of its own rather than something the order does for you.
steps.because: there is a check for whether an offer can be accepted (CanAcceptOffer)

steps.do: Look for the offer where it is announced instead of hunting through the menus.
steps.because: an offer is announced with an indicator and a canvas of its own (WholesaleOfferIndicator, WholeSaleOfferCanvas)

steps.do: Expect online orders to carry their own offer indicator as well.
steps.because: online orders have their own offer indicator (OnlineOrderOfferIndicator)

steps.do: Keep discounts apart from offers, because they are a separate system with their own panel and rate.
steps.because: discounts have their own manager, panel, current value and rate (DiscountManager, DiscountPanel, currentDiscount, discountRate, isDiscount)

steps.do: Use the bulk discount rather than assuming it, because buying in bulk carries a ratio of its own.
steps.because: bulk buying carries a discount ratio of its own (bulkDiscountRatio)

steps.do: In a shared shop, agree who is taking the offer, because the offer screen is shared too.
steps.because: the wholesale manager and its offer canvas have networked forms (NetworkWholeSaleManager, NetworkWholeSaleOfferCanvas)

commonMistakes: Ordering first and reading the offer afterwards.
Treating a discount and an offer as the same thing and doubling up by accident.
Missing the time limit and finding the offer gone when the order is placed.
Buying a bulk lot that is cheap per unit and expensive in shelf space.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
